react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is dominated by steroid hormone biosynthesis and interconversion, with convergent evidence from three independent paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-network analysis). Five C19/C18 steroid intermediates are the primary driver metabolites: dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227), androstenedione (KEGG:C00280), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), estrone (KEGG:C00468), and estradiol (KEGG:C00951). These five compounds achieve a top-ranked hit across every tool — RaMP ORA reports the Sulfatase and aromatase pathway (WP:WP5368, FDR 7.99×10⁻¹⁶, 5/14 pathway members) and the Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism KEGG map (map00150, FDR 6.44×10⁻¹⁵, 5/27); MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirms steroid hormone biosynthesis (KEGG:hsa00140, p=8.39×10⁻⁶, 5/87); mummichog reports androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=1.68×10⁻⁴, 11/11 network nodes). The consistent 5-compound overlap across all methods points to a coordinated perturbation of the aromatase (CYP19A1) and 17β-HSD axis. Three peripheral compounds — indoleacetaldehyde (tryptophan metabolism), menadione (no enrichment), and (S)-3-hydroxyisobutyric acid (valine/propanoate metabolism) — appear at marginal significance and likely reflect secondary metabolic consequences of the primary steroid imbalance.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is dominated by steroid hormone biosynthesis and interconversion, with convergent evidence from three independent paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-network analysis). Five C19/C18 steroid intermediates are the primary driver metabolites: dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227), androstenedione (KEGG:C00280), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), estrone (KEGG:C00468), and estradiol (KEGG:C00951). These five compounds achieve a top-ranked hit across every tool — RaMP ORA reports the Sulfatase and aromatase pathway (WP:WP5368, FDR 7.99×10⁻¹⁶, 5/14 pathway members) and the Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism KEGG map (map00150, FDR 6.44×10⁻¹⁵, 5/27); MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirms steroid hormone biosynthesis (KEGG:hsa00140, p=8.39×10⁻⁶, 5/87); mummichog reports androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=1.68×10⁻⁴, 11/11 network nodes). The consistent 5-compound overlap across all methods points to a coordinated perturbation of the aromatase (CYP19A1) and 17β-HSD axis. Three peripheral compounds — indoleacetaldehyde (tryptophan metabolism), menadione (no enrichment), and (S)-3-hydroxyisobutyric acid (valine/propanoate metabolism) — appear at marginal significance and likely reflect secondary metabolic consequences of the primary steroid imbalance.
